question: Select the correct option for precipitation reaction.

options.text: One reactant should be a carbon compound.
Solid mass separates out on mixing two clear solutions.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid mass separates out on mixing two clear solutions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This is the defining feature of a precipitation reaction, where **an insoluble solid **(precipitate) forms when two aqueous solutions are mixed.
 
• The precipitate separates from the solution and often appears as a **cloudy or solid mass** that sinks to the bottom.
 
• Precipitation reactions occur because one of the products is** insoluble in water, causing it to separate out from the solution.**
 
• Precipitation reactions are used to remove **unwanted ions from water **by forming insoluble compounds that can be filtered out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acid-Base Reaction** Involves the transfer of a proton (H⁺) from an acid to a base.
 
• **Neutralization Reaction** A reaction between an acid and a base to produce salt and water.
 
• **Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions**:
 
 
• **Exothermic Reaction: **Releases energy, usually in the form of heat (e.g., combustion).
 
• **Endothermic Reaction: **Absorbs energy from its surroundings (e.g., photosynthesis).
 
 
 
• **Redox (Oxidation-Reduction) Reaction** A reaction where one substance is oxidized (loses electrons) and another is reduced (gains electrons).
